director.chapterArc: Chapter 4 — The Door That Opened Anyway
director.restraintNote: The scene escalates from procedural anxiety to chaotic combat, then snaps into a surreal, silent transformation. Maintain the narrator's grounded, arithmetic voice throughout; do not let the magic feel wondrous or terrifying in an emotional sense, but rather as a sudden physical fact that overrides all prior logic.

cues.delivery: Mother's voice is flat and ordinary despite the situation; Callie reports it with clinical distance.
cues.from: It lasted a little under two minutes, and for most of it Callie was not in her own body at all. Her mother lay on the wagon boards with her eyes half open and did not answer to her name, and her right hand went on doing a small plucking motion at the blanket, over and over, the same motion, as if she were picking at a thread that was not there. Then she stopped. Then she took a long breath and looked up at all four of them standing over her and said, in a perfectly ordinary voice, "What."
cues.through: "What," her mother said again, and then, with the first edge of something under it, "Callie, what."
cues.reason: Establishes the baseline of 'new' sickness without melodrama.

cues.delivery: Callie's dialogue is precise and tactical; Katori's questions are flat imperatives. The tension comes from the geometry of the threat.
cues.through: "You heard me. I'm not asking you what's dangerous, I know what's dangerous. I'm asking you which of the two things we can actually do is worse. On the causeway at dusk, or camped on this pan, beside a line, in the dark, until morning."
cues.reason: The decision to cross at dusk requires absolute clarity on the stakes.

cues.delivery: Shift from singular threat to mass; voice tightens as Callie realizes the scale.
cues.from: Because the first one was not one. The first one was the first, which is a completely different thing, and by the time it got its hands over the shoulder of the embankment there were four more below it on the east rock and six on the west and a long smear of movement out on the pan that Callie could not count and did not try to.
cues.through: "Mass on the west," she said. Her voice came out much steadier than she was. "West is the mass. East is three, four — east is small."
cues.reason: The realization that 'the first one was not one' is a tactical pivot.

cues.delivery: Combat mechanics described with staccato precision; 'unhappen' is a physical observation.
cues.from: The first one at her end came over the shoulder on the east side with its long arms out and its head down, and she did not swing at it. She put the hook over the top of its shoulder from the outside, set her back foot on the road, and leaned, and the whole weight of it went back the way it had come.
cues.through: It did not matter. It had cost her one second and a pull, and it had cost them ninety feet of climbing, and while they were climbing they were not on her road.
cues.reason: Establish the physics of the hook before introducing the ash trap.

cues.delivery: Callie's shout is a desperate command; Katori's killing is efficient and terrifyingly bright. The ash trap realization must feel like a stomach drop.
cues.from: "Don't kill them," she shouted forward. "Tip them — don't kill them —"
cues.reason: The 'trap' moment requires the narrator to convey Callie's sudden understanding of her own mistake.

cues.delivery: The mule falling is a sharp cut; Callie's descent for the hook is frantic but physical.
cues.from: The mule went over at about the four-minute mark.
cues.through: It took eleven seconds and it was the stupidest thing she had ever done. She went down on three points the way they did, and got her boot wedged, and got it back, and reached the hook and hauled it out of the slabs with both hands and a noise she did not hear herself make.
cues.reason: Maintain the rhythm of action without letting it become generic chaos.

cues.delivery: Mother's voice is a whisper of dread; Callie runs with desperate focus.
cues.from: She was starting back up when her mother said her name.
cues.reason: The mother's call cuts through the noise as a specific emotional anchor.

cues.delivery: The horse kick is described with brutal physical clarity; the impact on Callie's shield must feel like a solid wall.
cues.from: She went up the near side, past the wheel, past the crates, past Ines coming the other way with a skillet in both hands, and she did not look at the horse because the horse was not the thing that was killing her mother, and that was the entire mistake and it was a completely reasonable one.
cues.through: The horse came off it. Four hundred kilos of animal at the end of a full kick rebounded off a thirteen-year-old girl standing in a road, and staggered sideways into the pole with her hindquarters, and screamed.
cues.reason: The transformation moment requires absolute lack of wonder or fear in the narration.

cues.delivery: Callie's internal realization is cold and factual; the hook transformation is described as a physical extension of her body.
cues.from: Callie stood with her arms still up over her face and her eyes still shut.
cues.through: She could see perfectly well through it. She had walked eleven paces in it and it had come with her, every step, the way a coat comes with you. The ash running down the camber of the road reached her boots and did not touch them. It parted, and went around her, and closed up again on the downhill side, and left her standing in a clean dry shape of road exactly the size of a girl.
cues.reason: The 'double Kindling' must be read as a discovered reality, not magic.

cues.delivery: Callie's voice breaks slightly on the realization; Katori's silence is heavy and absolute.
cues.from: She was holding both of them. At the same time. She could feel the weight of each one separately, and she knew — without one single person ever having told her anything about any of it — that she was not supposed to be able to.
cues.through: She did not answer her for a long time, and the not-answering went on and on, out there in the dark in the middle of two miles of road with nowhere at either end of it to turn around — while the ash came down the camber and parted around a girl's boots and closed up behind them, and the hook her grandfather had used to swing grain sacks went on being four feet longer than it had ever been in its life.
cues.reason: The ending must land in a state of unresolved clarity.

pauses.after: It lasted a little under two minutes, and for most of it Callie was not in her own body at all. Her mother lay on the wagon boards with her eyes half open and did not answer to her name, and her right hand went on doing a small plucking motion at the blanket, over and over, the same motion, as if she were picking at a thread that was not there. Then she stopped. Then she took a long breath and looked up at all four of them standing over her and said, in a perfectly ordinary voice, "What."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Mother's first line; allows the 'ordinary' tone to register.

pauses.after: "Everywhere. That's the problem." Callie crouched and drew it in the dust with the end of the hook, because she needed her hands doing something. "The whole flat drains north-east. Everything that comes across this country comes across that, and it walks the low pan until it hits the embankment, and the embankment's the only grade in eleven miles. So it goes up. It always goes up. This isn't a line crossing the road, it's — the road is where the line ends up."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the road geometry before Katori asks the next question.
Emphasizes the binary choice that drives the scene's tension.

pauses.after: "The causeway," she said. "There's no turning on it. If it's bad in the middle we go forward or we go nowhere, and I want that said before anybody agrees with me."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Callie's decision; marks the point of no return.

pauses.after: And that was the last decision anybody got to make with time to spare in it.
pauses.reason: Pause before the escalation from 'one' to 'mass'. A breath for the realization.
Isolates the physical action of leverage before describing the result.

pauses.after: That was the trap and there was no way out through the front of it.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on the trap; allows the weight of Callie's mistake to settle before she screams.
Emphasizes the desperate command against Katori's action.

pauses.after: "None," said Ines, eight seconds later, and put the bow down on the crates with a care that under any other circumstances would have been funny, and picked up the skillet.
pauses.reason: Completed thought after Ines switches weapons; transition into the mule falling.
Isolates Callie's lack of agency in her desperate move.

pauses.after: It took eleven seconds and it was the stupidest thing she had ever done. She went down on three points the way they did, and got her boot wedged, and got it back, and reached the hook and hauled it out of the slabs with both hands and a noise she did not hear herself make.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on Callie's retrieval of the hook and her mother's call. A breath for the shift in focus.
Emphasizes the irony and tragedy of Callie's action regarding the horse.
Isolates the physical impossibility of the kick stopping.

pauses.after: The horse came off it. Four hundred kilos of animal at the end of a full kick rebounded off a thirteen-year-old girl standing in a road, and staggered sideways into the pole with her hindquarters, and screamed.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after the horse screams; transition to Callie standing still.

pauses.after: The last of the light was off the pan. The causeway ran north into blue dark in front of them and south into blue dark behind them, and there was ash lying silver in every seam of it for forty paces in both directions.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the scene's atmosphere before focusing on Callie alone.

pauses.before: not supposed to be able to
pauses.reason: Emphasizes the core realization that breaks Callie's understanding of her world.
